onEnter.speaker: none
onEnter.t: Both the men's and women's locker rooms are quiet, with only one officer on duty. Andy Liu is pacing anxiously by the door.

hotspots.title: Victor's Locker
hotspots.desc: In the late Victor Jiang's locker are two of his shirts, a cartoon charm, a park logo commemorative stamp, and a sheet of park stationery covered with many park logo stamps. Dates are handwritten beside them, and they seem to overlap with the haunted house performance dates.

hotspots.title: Sunny's Locker
hotspots.desc: In Sunny Chen's locker are a warm yellow dress, a pair of high heels, a children's toy, a park logo commemorative stamp, and a postcard covered with many park logo stamps. The postcard is a giveaway from a milk tea brand.

hotspots.title: Aiden's Locker
hotspots.desc: In Aiden Li's locker are two T-shirts printed with the park logo and a pair of black trousers.

hotspots.title: Faye's Locker
hotspots.desc: In Faye Liu's locker are a white T-shirt, a pair of jeans, and a cat-head volunteer badge with the word SWEET on it. There is an accident investigation report from one year ago; it analyzes in detail the cause of the May 2, 2024 float parade accident: an aging battery short-circuited. There is also a bottle of sertraline (an anti-anxiety medication), prescribed three months ago, with more than half the bottle already taken.

onEnter.speaker: char_meiyu
onEnter.t: Victor Jiang... is he really dead?

onEnter.speaker: char_meiyu
onEnter.t: Oh my god, that is horrifying.

introDialogue.speaker: none
introDialogue.t: October 28, 2025, 12:30 PM, Chaoye Park, Performer Locker Room

char_mingqi.speaker: none
char_mingqi.t: Celeste Ming looks like he has absolutely no intention of talking.

char_shihui.speaker: char_shihui
char_shihui.t: Hey, Sylva, good to see you again. Feel free to ask whatever you need.

dialogue.speaker: char_andy
dialogue.t: Following Officer Lyra Qin's instructions, we opened Victor Jiang's locker. Then we also asked Sunny Chen, Aiden Li, and Faye Liu to open their lockers so we could inspect them.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Anything strange?

dialogue.speaker: char_andy
dialogue.t: Mostly changes of clothes, personal items, documents, medicine, that kind of thing.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: All right, I will take a look myself. Also, yesterday Officer Lyra Qin mentioned that a visitor lost something in the haunted house. What was that about?

dialogue.speaker: char_andy
dialogue.t: Ah... actually, it has already been found. There is a small pavilion near the haunted house. When the visitor who lost the item called it, the ringtone went off, and a visitor resting there heard a sound in the grass behind them. They quickly picked it up and handed it to staff.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: What time was that?

dialogue.speaker: char_andy
dialogue.t: It was a little after ten. Once we found it, we contacted the visitor right away, got their address, and mailed it to them.

dialogue.speaker: char_andy
dialogue.t: Officer Lyra Qin said that after you finish checking here, you can go to the temporary interrogation area. Celeste Ming and Faye Liu should already be there.

dialogue.speaker: char_andy
dialogue.t: Oh, right. Officer Lyra Qin asked us to investigate Victor's office computer, email, and so on. This may interest you.

dialogue.speaker: char_andy
dialogue.t: Need any help? If it's about park stuff, please feel free to ask.

dialogue.speaker: char_andy
dialogue.t: Faye's locker? Is there something here that caught your interest?

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: The one that caught my attention is...

options.text: A. The cat-head volunteer badge with the word SWEET on it
options.reply: This one? I haven't seen it before either.

options.text: B. The float parade accident report
C. Sertraline
options.reply: It seems the performers really are under a lot of pressure...

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Do you remember anything about this accident investigation report? The date is May 2, 2024.

dialogue.speaker: char_andy
dialogue.t: I do. It was during a holiday, and one of the parade floats suddenly made a loud bang and gave off a huge cloud of white smoke. Faye was on the carriage where the accident happened, and it scared her badly. The investigation result was just as this report says.

dialogue.speaker: char_andy
dialogue.t: There was even a public criticism notice at the time. The colleague responsible for maintenance inspections had a large bonus deducted. The incident had quite an impact. The park called everyone into meetings several times, and it also made it standard policy to hold at least four safety trainings every year.

dialogue.speaker: char_meiyu
dialogue.t: I am Faye Liu, a dancer. I mainly work the day shift. For night shifts, I am a temporary performer for the haunted house project, and I go onstage if needed.

dialogue.speaker: char_meiyu
dialogue.t: I've been working at the park for four years.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: If you have worked here for four years, did you know anything about the haunted house performer group when the project first started three years ago?

dialogue.speaker: char_meiyu
dialogue.t: Yes. At first, former Performance Department director Celeste Ming led it, wrote the proposal, and submitted it. Then management assigned Victor Jiang to assist him.

dialogue.speaker: char_meiyu
dialogue.t: Sunny Chen had a good relationship with Victor Jiang, so she joined the project very early. Daniel Xiao was joined after Sunny Chen.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: So you knew Daniel Xiao too, right?

dialogue.speaker: char_meiyu
dialogue.t: Yes, I knew him...

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: What was your relationship like?

dialogue.speaker: char_meiyu
dialogue.t: Average, I guess...

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Do you know whether he had any family, friends, a lover, or anything like that?

dialogue.speaker: char_meiyu
dialogue.t: I don't know about that.

dialogue.speaker: char_meiyu
dialogue.t: Aiden Li came later. At first he was something like stage crew and prop master? Something like that? Then he became a performer.

dialogue.speaker: char_meiyu
dialogue.t: Just colleagues. He was always in the team leader role, so in practice maybe we counted as supervisor and subordinate?

dialogue.speaker: char_meiyu
dialogue.t: My mother was sick, so I went back to my hometown, Hexi City, and stayed with her for two days.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: What time was your train, exactly?

dialogue.speaker: char_meiyu
dialogue.t: My outbound train left at 9 a.m. on the 27th, and my return train was at 9 this morning.

dialogue.speaker: char_meiyu
dialogue.t: I feel that once you're home, you should spend proper time with your family, so I barely looked at my phone. I only found out last night that something had happened to Victor Jiang.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: What happened in that float parade accident on May 2, 2024?

dialogue.speaker: char_meiyu
dialogue.t: Ah... it was just a regular accident. Things like that happen all the time. It wasn't a big deal.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: But according to security staff, it wasn't an ordinary accident. It had a major impact, and the park even increased the number of safety training sessions each year because of it.

dialogue.speaker: char_meiyu
dialogue.t: Mm... that's true, but it was a long time ago. I've almost forgotten about it...

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: If you've forgotten it, then why were you looking through the accident investigation report from that year?

dialogue.speaker: char_meiyu
dialogue.t: Recently... I happened to get hold of it.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: You were badly frightened, weren't you?

dialogue.speaker: char_meiyu
dialogue.t: Yes... After that, even loud noises would make me jump.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: So after that, you needed to take anti-anxiety medication?

dialogue.speaker: char_meiyu
dialogue.t: Yes...

dialogue.speaker: char_meiyu
dialogue.t: Director Shi didn't make things difficult for me at the time, either. And that was the end of it.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Ray Shi said he never intended to make things difficult for you in the first place.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: The reason you thought Ray Shi would make things difficult for you was actually...

choices.question: The reason you thought Ray Shi would make things difficult for you was actually...

options.text: A Victor told you Ray was furious
B Ray looked furious
C You thought the accident was your fault

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: You thought this accident had something to do with what you did.

dialogue.speaker: char_meiyu
dialogue.t: What I did? What did I do?

options.text: A You placed the headpiece above the battery
B You made a mistake during the performance
C You failed to do a safety check before the show
options.reply: I was just an actor. I wasn't responsible for safety checks...

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: The park's custom-made headpiece was ignited and destroyed by the fire from the battery's spontaneous combustion. According to the accident investigation report, it wasn't your fault at all. Any normal person would think that, wouldn't they?

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: That makes Victor Jiang's actions very suspicious. Why would he deliberately tell Ray Shi, right in front of you, not to punish you?

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: If I'm guessing correctly, what Victor actually wanted was...

options.text: A To ease your anxiety
B To show his concern for a colleague
C To make you feel indebted to him

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Victor wanted you to think he had solved a big problem for you, didn't he?

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Until recently, when you realized that what Victor told you back then didn't match the actual findings of the accident investigation. Right? That's why you copied that report.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: And if I'm not mistaken, you've already confirmed the real cause of the accident with the staff member who issued the report, haven't you?

dialogue.speaker: char_meiyu
dialogue.t: Yes.

t_meiyu_real_accident_reason.title: The Real Cause of the Accident

dialogue.speaker: char_meiyu
dialogue.t: You're right.

dialogue.speaker: char_meiyu
dialogue.t: I found the investigation report for that accident, made a copy, and took it to ask the staff member who had been in charge of the investigation at the time.

dialogue.speaker: char_meiyu
dialogue.t: He said it really was battery aging. I asked whether it had anything to do with the headpiece that caught fire. He said there was some connection, but not much. That battery's internal resistance had already severely exceeded the acceptable limit. Even if nothing had been placed on it, it still might have combusted on its own.

dialogue.speaker: char_meiyu
dialogue.t: But that wasn't what Victor told me at the time. He said I had no common sense, that I put the heavy performance headpiece on top of the battery compartment and blocked the battery's heat dissipation, and that this was the main cause of the accident.

dialogue.speaker: char_meiyu
dialogue.t: He said he was on good terms with people in the maintenance department and would help me change the investigation report so it said the battery had combusted on its own. That way, the park wouldn't come after me. And he told me never to mention it to anyone again.

dialogue.speaker: char_meiyu
dialogue.t: I really believed that explanation, and I lived in fear and guilt all this time.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: So you did have a reason to resent Victor Jiang, didn't you?

dialogue.speaker: char_meiyu
dialogue.t: After seeing the truth, I was indeed furious, but I'm not the killer! How could I kill someone over something like this?

dialogue.speaker: char_meiyu
dialogue.t: If we're talking about someone more likely to have been angered by Victor and acted on it, wouldn't that actually be Aiden?

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Why Aiden Li?

dialogue.speaker: char_meiyu
dialogue.t: Because of what Victor used to say... Victor often joked about that incident...

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: What joke?

dialogue.speaker: char_meiyu
dialogue.t: Victor said more than once while drinking with other people that Aiden was getting more and more skilled at pulling ropes, no wonder he had practice on a real person.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: What? Was he implying... that Aiden Li had something to do with Daniel Xiao's death?

dialogue.speaker: char_meiyu
dialogue.t: It's probably exactly what you're thinking.

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: I'm a theater director. I used to be the overall performance designer at this park. Later, for certain reasons, I left.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: What reasons?

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: You already know, don't you? Otherwise you wouldn't have come to me, right?

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Could you explain it yourself?

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: Then let me ask you: what do you think the reason was? Hm?

choices.question: What do you think the reason was?

options.text: A Harassment
B Bullying
C Daniel Xiao's death

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: The park believes I should be held responsible for actor Daniel Xiao's death. I was deeply upset that something like that happened in the team, but I don't agree that it was my fault. I also do not agree with how the park handled it.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: How did the park handle it?

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: How else? They had a talk with me and said the incident reflected badly on everyone. If the park stepped in to dismiss me, they said it would only make things more humiliating for me.

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: In short, they persuaded me to resign voluntarily.

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: To be honest, I didn't want to stay there anymore anyway. That place was rotten from top to bottom. It was not worth any more of my valuable time.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: So you left voluntarily?

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: Yes. I also had some theater work to deal with at the time, so I just left. The park's official notice did not name me, so that was that. I did not care anymore.

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: As for anything else, it has nothing to do with me.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Someone said one reason you left was that you had harassed female performers.

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: Hah. I have been gone for so long, and people are still spouting nonsense about that?

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: I never harassed anyone, all right?

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: If you did not do it, didn't you want to clear things up?

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: Hmph... That kind of absurd rumor was not worth responding to at all.

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: Why should I have to clarify something I never did in the first place?

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: Aren't you looking into Victor's death? Then why are you picking on me?

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: He used to be my subordinate. Rough around the edges, but quite capable.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Rough around the edges?

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: Yes. He was practically like some street punk. Smoking, drinking, acting like best buddies with everyone. At every meeting, he would slump sideways in his chair and look at people out of the corner of his eye.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Did he treat you badly?

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: Hah, badly is putting it mildly. That man always looked down on the scripts I wrote.

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: When I tried to discuss serious work with him and explain my ideas and the overall arrangements, he would answer in that snide, roundabout way of his. He wouldn't listen or do the work.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Sounds like he did not respect your authority very much.

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: Exactly. The key point is, he really did have a bunch of followers who did whatever he said. That tells you what kind of people work at this park. It made some of my original designs impossible to realize.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Then what did you mean by quite capable?

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: To be fair and objective, when it came to the parts of the work he was interested in, he was beyond reproach.

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: His control over the precision of the performances and his creativity with costumes, makeup, and props exceeded my expectations.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Was he the one who designed the use of the dolls too?

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: Yes. Those things should originally have been under my control, but he relied on his good relationship with the props team to shut me out. I was quite angry at first, but later I felt he did seem suited to that kind of work. For example, attaching doll props to the waist for a duet and so on. Those ideas were rather interesting.

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: I often saw him drilling movements and rehearsing with the performers over and over. The effect was good. So I let him be, and it lightened my workload a bit too.

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: But when it came to Daniel Xiao... that man really did put me in a terrible position.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Was it because of this?

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: Where... where did you find that?

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: On his office computer. He had kept this email the whole time, and even starred it.

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: I was at home writing scripts. You are not treating me as a suspect, are you?

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: Why did you bring me in for something like this? Shouldn't you be investigating that relative of the board member?

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Who?

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: Victor Jiang was against me because he thought he could take my job, right? And look what happened—I left, and they brought in some guy with connections. You should be looking into him, not me.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Wait. Do you mean Ray Shi, the current head of the Performance Department?

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: Yeah. He's the nephew of one of the board members—Director Li. You didn't know that? Knowing Victor's personality, those two must have clashed. That's the guy you should be looking into, not me.

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: Of course I mean the fact that I was forced to resign because of Daniel Xiao's death.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Why did everyone think you were responsible for his death?

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: How would I know? I only watched him rehearse a couple of times and yelled at him a few times. Wasn't he supposed to be a top student from Jiangpu Dance Academy? With that kind of performance, it's just unacceptable.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: So you were pressuring him, then?

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: Hah. Isn't that all perfectly normal work communication? If someone cannot even take that much, they might as well not come to work.

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: I do not think I should be held responsible for his death at all.

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: But Victor Jiang never clarified the matter. Of course, that was exactly what I expected. I knew he would love to see me suffer.

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: Then again, I think the whole thing sounds absurd in itself. The real reason Daniel Xiao killed himself had nothing to do with me, did it? Maybe it was something in his family. Maybe someone dumped him.

dialogue.speaker: char_mingqi
dialogue.t: No one considered possibilities like that. And as for the claim that I harassed people, is there any evidence? It is all one-sided talk. In reality, no one actually wanted to get to the bottom of anything, did they?

dialogue.speaker: char_shihui
dialogue.t: Hm? You met Celeste Ming? Well? Do you think he is that kind of hypocritical person? Did he admit what happened back then?

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: I asked Celeste Ming why he left the park. He said it was because Daniel Xiao died and the park needed a scapegoat. It had nothing to do with the harassment incident you mentioned.

dialogue.speaker: char_shihui
dialogue.t: Ah... is that so? I see...

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: So what was the harassment you mentioned about?

dialogue.speaker: char_shihui
dialogue.t: It was just something I heard. A person who worked at the park posted anonymously on social media, saying that a certain park leader had harassed female performers.

dialogue.speaker: char_shihui
dialogue.t: Some people guessed it was Celeste Ming and asked leading questions about it, but the poster never came forward to clarify... Celeste also did not say anything, so it seemed to become accepted as fact...

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: He only never refuted it publicly. That does not prove he did those things. The truth was never properly investigated, was it? Was there some other reason the park was so eager to pin every bad thing on him?

dialogue.speaker: char_shihui
dialogue.t: Sigh... well... some things are hard to talk about...

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Why are they hard to talk about?

dialogue.speaker: char_shihui
dialogue.t: Actually, your guess is right... Celeste Ming really was targeted from all sides... In the park, even though his position was high, he was always relatively isolated.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Why was that?

dialogue.speaker: char_shihui
dialogue.t: Alright, I'll be straight with you...

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: What happened with the parade float battery explosion on May 2, 2024?

dialogue.speaker: char_shihui
dialogue.t: Oh, that incident. I remember it. A float's battery really did suddenly explode, and it gave everyone quite a scare.

dialogue.speaker: char_shihui
dialogue.t: Why are you suddenly asking about that?

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: I found the accident investigation report from back then in Faye's locker. It happened a year ago, so I am curious why Faye has that report now.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: What exactly happened?

dialogue.speaker: char_shihui
dialogue.t: It was between parade performances. Suddenly there was a bang, like something exploding. When I rushed over, the whole carriage was almost covered in white smoke, and there were flames at the rear. Later we found out that Faye's performance prop at the back of the float had caught fire.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: What kind of performance prop was it?

dialogue.speaker: char_shihui
dialogue.t: A cartoon mascot head used for performances, custom-made by the park, and pretty expensive. Victor even came over to tell me not to blame Faye for it, and not to penalize her. But honestly, I didn't think an actor should be punished for that in the first place. If an actor had been hurt, that would have been far more serious than a burned mascot head.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Wait, why did Victor assume you would punish her?

dialogue.speaker: char_shihui
dialogue.t: Probably because that mascot head was an important prop and got burned? That's just my guess. To be honest, I don't understand why Victor said that either, especially right in front of Faye. It made it sound like I was going to deliberately make things difficult for her.

dialogue.speaker: char_shihui
dialogue.t: Well... I learned about this from a relative who works at the park. Celeste Ming came here because the park was undergoing reforms at the time, and the board had decided to overhaul all of the park's entertainment projects.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: A relative...are you talking about Ms Li from the board?

dialogue.speaker: char_shihui
dialogue.t: Ahahaha, yes... how did you know?

dialogue.speaker: char_shihui
dialogue.t: The park specifically poached Celeste Ming from ArcLight Group, a major entertainment company. His resume and education were both extremely impressive. Celeste Ming really is very capable, but after he arrived, he had quite a few conflicts with the park's management.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: What kind of conflicts?

dialogue.speaker: char_shihui
dialogue.t: The park thought Celeste's proposals were too aggressive and too expensive. Chaoye Park doesn't have as much money as those entertainment companies, after all. A lot of the resources just couldn't be provided.

dialogue.speaker: char_shihui
dialogue.t: The only project that was actually implemented was the haunted house. The float parade was also planned by him, but it wasn't officially carried out until after he left.

dialogue.speaker: char_shihui
dialogue.t: Maybe it was just a bad fit. Celeste Ming was clearly losing more and more motivation here.

dialogue.speaker: char_shihui
dialogue.t: Later, he started taking outside work, and sometimes no one would see him for an entire day. Because his rank was very high, and the park had paid a lot to bring him in, the administration department didn't really dare to manage him.

dialogue.speaker: char_shihui
dialogue.t: After the board found out, they kept wanting to find a reason to dismiss him, but that would have been like slapping themselves in the face...

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: So they chose to let the matter go cold. When public opinion turned against him, they didn't step forward to defend him, and once the Daniel Xiao incident happened, they used the opportunity to get rid of this huge problem. Is that right?

dialogue.speaker: char_shihui
dialogue.t: Yes...

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Then, under those circumstances, one thing becomes highly suspicious.

options.text: A. The identity of the person who posted the accusation
options.reply: Ah, is there any connection between those two things?

options.text: B. Accountability for Daniel Xiao's death
C. The real reason for the bullying
options.reply: Huh? What are you talking about?

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: The park wanted to use Daniel Xiao's death as a reason to fire Celeste Ming. So maybe, strictly speaking, Celeste wasn't really the one to blame for it in the first place.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: You also said Celeste Ming was often out and not working in the park. Could a few reprimands really have driven Daniel Xiao to suicide? That sounds extremely hard to believe.

dialogue.speaker: char_shihui
dialogue.t: Ah, now that you mention it, that's true...

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Then, if we don't treat Celeste Ming as the person primarily responsible, the person who truly should have been held responsible for Daniel Xiao's death might be that person.

choices.question: Who truly should have been held responsible for Daniel Xiao's death?

options.text: A. Sunny Chen
B. Victor Jiang
C. Faye Liu

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Victor Jiang was in charge of rehearsals and managed many of the practical details of the performances.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Logically, if an actor hanged himself at a performance venue, Victor Jiang should have been the person primarily responsible. Why did he disappear from the matter?

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: If we think about it from that angle, the killer's motive for murdering Victor Jiang might have been...

choices.question: The killer's motive for murdering Victor Jiang might have been...

options.text: A. Jealousy
options.reply: Huh? What are you talking about...

options.text: B. Silencing him
options.reply: You mean the killer murdered two people...?

options.text: C. Revenge

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: The killer probably believed the victim had directly or indirectly caused Daniel Xiao's death.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: So the killer chose the haunted house, the same place where the incident happened back then, and murdered Victor Jiang in the same way.

dialogue.speaker: char_shihui
dialogue.t: Oh my god... who could it be?

dialogue.speaker: char_shihui
dialogue.t: Oh, suspects? Look, we're a good team. There's no way something like that happened.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: What do you mean, a good team? Stop kidding yourself...

dialogue.speaker: char_shihui
dialogue.t: Then tell me, leaving aside anyone outside the team for now, who is suspicious?

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: The suspicious people might have two kinds of motives. First, believing Daniel Xiao's death was connected to Victor Jiang. Second, already having issues with Victor Jiang's behavior. For example, Aiden Li.

dialogue.speaker: char_shihui
dialogue.t: Aiden? How is that possible...

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Victor Jiang would occasionally hint, as a joke over drinks, that Aiden Li was connected to Daniel Xiao's death. So what exactly happened back then?

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Also, Faye Liu too.

dialogue.speaker: char_shihui
dialogue.t: Faye is suspicious too...?

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Yes. As we just discussed, the float parade accident was investigated and found not to be Faye's fault at all. But under Victor Jiang's misleading influence, Faye believed she had caused the accident, and she began developing compulsive behaviors and anxiety, so bad that she had to take medication.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Because they both knew Daniel Xiao, they may also have had a motive for revenge. But beyond that, we also need to investigate Daniel Xiao's relationships.

dialogue.speaker: char_shihui
dialogue.t: Ah... is that so...

dialogue.speaker: char_qin
dialogue.t: Looks like there is still a lot to investigate.

dialogue.speaker: char_qin
dialogue.t: I've already sent people to investigate Daniel Xiao's relationships before his death. There may be some new leads tomorrow. Also, an officer just spoke with Faye Liu's mother and confirmed that Faye and her mother really have been together these past two days.

dialogue.speaker: char_qin
dialogue.t: And regarding Daniel Xiao's death, I think we need to conduct a second round of questioning with Sunny Chen and Aiden Li.

dialogue.speaker: char_qin
dialogue.t: Then let's leave this stage of the investigation here for now. Based on the clues we obtained today, we'll proceed with the next round of verification and questioning. Sylva, see you tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Why did Victor Jiang say those suggestive things to Aiden Li? Why did he make Faye Liu believe she had made a serious mistake at work?

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: The events from three years ago are gradually surfacing, but questions keep emerging one after another.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: If this really is about revenge, the killer should be someone close to Daniel Xiao.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Why was the killer convinced that Victor Jiang was the one who caused Daniel Xiao's death? And how did the killer commit the crime during the performance?

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: What we need to investigate now is not only the suspects in the case before us, but also the truth behind Daniel Xiao's suicide three years ago.

dialogue.speaker: none
dialogue.t: Tomorrow, let's verify each of these questions one by one.
